thread:
lia: Heads up — we're seeing a spike in GPU pending pods in ap-southeast1b starting ~10m ago. Schedulers showing a LOT of small pod churn.
lia: Console shows 12% drop in available GPU slots vs baseline, network errors ~conntrack spikes in that AZ.
sam: is this the nvlink/egress thing again?
jon: I see the same. kube-scheduler logs show repeated Preempt calls then immediate requeue: 'failed to allocate: affinity conflicts' + 'taint:cold-node not tolerated'.
maya: tagging in ML load — some training jobs are small <0.5 GPU and are getting shuffled across nodes, causing fragmentation.
lia: here's the one-line from scheduler: 
```
I0518 14:22:01.123456 1 scheduling_queue.go:... Pod preempted: reason=AffinityConflict node=ap-se1b-node-172
```
jon: also noticed network attach latencies to warm nodes are high, pods can't attach to NIC in time so attach-detach flaps. That leaks ephemeral allocations.
sam: repro steps I ran: `kubectl get pods -n ml -o wide | grep Pending` shows many stuck with `0/1 nodes available: node(s) had taint {warm=false}, affinity not match`
lia: ops-bot shows recent maintenance on ap-southeast1b router ~14:10 that may have increased attach latency. ops-bot: `maintenance: interconnect-dbi-3 — rolling update, expected 8m impact`.
maya: ok, so combined: NIC attach latency + small pods + strict anti-affinity => tiny pockets of unusable GPU. Cost impact: our telemetry reports ~15% effective capacity loss for those clusters => burned on-demand node spins.
jon: quick mitigation options: 1) temporarily relax anti-affinity rules for known training namespaces 2) increase warm pool size 3) increase `--eviction-pressure` grace window so we don't churn on transient taint flips.
sam: I'd add 4) lower fractional GPU request for batch jobs so they pack more densely (but that requires job changes).
lia: Can we do a fast emergency change: annotate the ml namespace with toleration to `warm-node` taint and bump warmpool by +3 nodes?
jon: +1 for warmpool bump. Toleration is risky for production but fine for a 30m window. I'll prepare the toleration snippet:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: ml
  annotations:
    infra/allow-warm-toleration: "true"
---
# Pod-level fallback
tolerations:
- key: "warm-node"
  operator: "Exists"
  effect: "NoSchedule"
  tolerationSeconds: 1800
```
sam: if we do tolerationSeconds it auto-expire — good idea. Also set scheduler plugin tweak? probably too risky for emergency.
maya: warmpool + tolerationSeconds 1800 sounds good. Also can we temporarily enable 'strict-packing=false' hint in the scheduler for small GPU pods?
lia: that's a config change, requires rollout. Not for emergency. We'll stick to warmpool + toleration + monitor.
jon: I'll submit the change to the autoscaler to bump warmpool target in ap-southeast1b from 6 -> 9 now.
jon: patch applied, autoscaler accepted the new target.
lia: I'll add the namespace annotation and patch 2 example deployments to include tolerationSeconds.
sam: monitoring watch: help me watch pod_pending_count and node_attach_latency dashboards. I'll set alerts low-threshold for 5m.
ops-bot: alert created: `ml-pod-pending-ap-se1b` threshold=30 pods for 5m -> notify #eng-platform.
maya: initial signs: pending pods dropping after warmpool nodes come up, attach latency decreasing.
lia: good. After 15m we should decide permanent changes: maybe soften anti-affinity heuristics or add a fractional-binpack admission.
sam: agree — long-term we should evaluate: 1) scheduler affinity scoring weight adjustments 2) a fractional GPU packing admission controller + eviction budget 3) better attach timeout & retry backoffs.
jon: action items captured: (1) revert toleration annotation after 30m (ops), (2) run a simulation of affinity-weight change in staging (sam + eng-sim), (3) design fractional packer RFC (maya + sam).
lia: ops — keep an eye on cost dashboard for the cluster. Warmpool + extra nodes will spike short-term cost. We're ok for now but call if >20% increase.
maya: noted. Thanks everyone.
lia: closing the thread once last pending drops below 5 for 10m.
sam: thanks — will follow up with RFC link later. :thumbsup:
